recent_posts.title: Formatting Data Links in Grafana Tables
recent_posts.summary: A practical walkthrough for formatting data links in Grafana table panels. By default, multiple data links in a table column produce an ugly pop-up instead of inline HTML links. The fix involves three steps: adding a new column via the 'Add field from calculation' transform (using Row index mode), applying a field override to set that column's cell type to 'Data links', and then removing data links from all other columns via field overrides. The result is a clean table with individual clickable links in a dedicated column.

recent_posts.title: Grafana Table Joins With SQL Expressions
recent_posts.summary: Grafana's SQL Expressions feature (available in Grafana 12 as optional, default in Grafana 13) lets you run SQL queries directly against the results of other queries in a panel. This replaces multiple data transformations with a single SQL JOIN, making it easier to combine Prometheus metrics like CPU and RAM into a unified table. You can also add extra columns for data links via the SELECT clause, eliminating the need for most transforms while retaining field overrides for formatting.

recent_posts.title: Creating Tables in Grafana From Multiple Prometheus Metrics
recent_posts.summary: A practical guide to building Grafana tables that combine multiple Prometheus metrics into a single view. Covers the step-by-step process: setting queries to Format:Table and Type:Instant, using the 'Merge series/tables' transform to join multiple queries, applying 'Organize fields by name' to rename and reorder columns, and using field overrides for per-column unit formatting. Uses Kubernetes CPU and memory metrics as concrete examples, and warns against using Join transforms which don't behave correctly for this use case.

recent_posts.title: Cascade River Road in HDR
recent_posts.summary: A personal photography outing to Cascade River Road in Marblemount, WA, showcasing HDR landscape images shot in winter conditions. The author explains the motivation for pursuing HDR photography given widespread modern display support, shares multiple images of fog, moss, streams, and snow, and notes that most shots were taken with a Hasselblad X2D II and 35-100mm zoom lens. Viewers are encouraged to use HDR-capable displays for the best experience.

recent_posts.title: The End of SRGB Is Neigh: HDR Images and Video on the Web in 2026
recent_posts.summary: The web has quietly moved beyond sRGB over the past few years, and it's now practical to publish HDR and wide-gamut images and video online. Modern displays (especially 4K TVs and Apple devices), cameras, browsers, and image formats like AVIF and JPEG XL all support HDR natively. The main bottleneck is no longer browsers or hardware but server-side tooling — image resizers, CMS platforms, and apps like Hugo, Immich, Slack, and YouTube's HDR transcoder still strip or ignore color profiles. The post explains color spaces (sRGB, Rec. 709, Rec. 2020, Rec. 2100, Display P3), why 8-bit JPEG/PNG fall short for HDR, how gain maps offer a JPEG workaround, and recommends AVIF + JPEG as the practical 2026 format pairing. Rec. 2100/HLG or PQ is suggested as the target color space going forward.

recent_posts.title: The Two-Mac HDMI CEC Problem
recent_posts.summary: M4 Macs with HDMI CEC support create conflicts when two are connected to the same Samsung TV, causing the display to repeatedly turn on and off. The issue stems from Macs reacting to each other's CEC messages with no way to configure the behavior. The HDMI CEC standard lacks proper usage policies, leading vendors to implement incompatible interpretations. The only workaround is power-cycling the TV when switching between Macs or disabling CEC entirely, as Apple provides no settings to control CEC behavior.

recent_posts.title: Testing slow motion HDR video at 240 FPS with Panasonic S1 II
recent_posts.summary: A slow-motion HDR video test of Eagle Falls shot at 240 FPS (239.76 FPS due to NTSC legacy standards) using a Panasonic S1 II camera. The author reflects on HDR rendering quality and the tradeoff between 1080P at 240 FPS versus 4K at 120 FPS for slow-motion capture.

recent_posts.title: Photographing the aurora with a fast lens
recent_posts.summary: A brief personal account of photographing the aurora borealis at night using a Sigma 14mm f/1.4 lens. The author discusses the challenges of focusing in low-light conditions with a fast lens shooting wide-open and expresses satisfaction with their night photography setup's exposure and focus results.

recent_posts.title: Shooting video at Cedar Creek Grist Mill with Blackmagic Pyxis 12k
recent_posts.summary: A photographer shares their experience shooting video at Cedar Creek Grist Mill in Washington, comparing results from a Panasonic GH6 to their new Blackmagic Pyxis 12k camera. The Pyxis delivers significantly better dynamic range and more reliable results despite having similar pixel sizes to the GH6. Shot at 8k 84 FPS and played back at 30 FPS for slow-motion effect, using a Zeiss Otus 28/1.4 lens. The author discusses their ongoing learning process with DaVinci Resolve for post-processing and color grading.

recent_posts.title: Trees in 8K
recent_posts.summary: A photographer shares their experience shooting 8K video with a Blackmagic Pyxis 12K camera (12,288x6,912 resolution) for use as Zoom meeting backgrounds. The video captures moss-covered trees near Squamish, BC, demonstrating extreme technical overkill since most video calls run at 720p or 1080p. The piece discusses the camera's 98-megapixel sensor, making it the highest-resolution 35mm format camera available today, and reflects on the creative process of capturing subtle, non-distracting landscape footage.

top_posts.title: Passwordless SSH and sudo with 1Password on Mac and Linux
top_posts.summary: A comprehensive guide to setting up passwordless SSH and sudo authentication using 1Password for SSH key management. The tutorial covers configuring 1Password's SSH agent, setting up SSH client configuration with agent forwarding, implementing pam_rssh for sudo authentication, and adding biometric authentication on Linux using Yubikey Bio. The approach eliminates the need to manually manage SSH keys across multiple systems while providing secure authentication through fingerprints or system biometrics.

top_posts.title: Client-side HTTP Metrics and Errors with Vector and Clickhouse
top_posts.summary: Enhancing website monitoring using Network Error Logging (NEL) allows you to collect HTTP errors and status updates from browsers without relying on Javascript. NEL, primarily supported by Chrome-family browsers, utilizes HTTP headers to send JSON status updates asynchronously. Implementing NEL with Clickhouse for data storage and Vector for data collection simplifies the process. Adding the necessary headers to the Caddy web server and using the recorded data helps in analyzing and improving web performance efficiently.

top_posts.title: Setting up GNSS/GPS on Intel E810-XXVDA4T Timing NICs
top_posts.summary: A comprehensive guide for configuring Intel E810-XXVDA4T timing NICs with GNSS/GPS capabilities as high-precision NTP time sources. Covers hardware setup, driver installation, GNSS module configuration in survey mode for fixed-position accuracy, and integration with Chrony for network time synchronization. The setup achieves nanosecond-level timing accuracy by combining GPS positioning, PTP hardware clocks, and proper software configuration on Ubuntu 24.04.

top_posts.title: Measured System Clock Frequency Stability in my Systems
top_posts.summary: The post discusses the challenges of maintaining accurate system clock frequencies across a variety of home servers. Despite significant skew in the clocks, ranging from 30 PPM fast to 60 PPM slow, Chrony effectively corrects inaccuracies by syncing with a reliable time source. It highlights the sensitivity of crystal oscillators to temperature changes, recommending TCXO or OCXO oscillators for improved accuracy.

top_posts.title: Home Ethernet 101
top_posts.summary: A comprehensive guide to planning and installing home network infrastructure during construction or renovation. Covers different levels of networking needs from basic WiFi to advanced fiber optic installations, with practical advice on cable types (Cat 6 vs Cat 6A), when to use fiber over copper, and future-proofing strategies. Includes detailed explanations of optical fiber standards, connector types, and considerations for different home networking scenarios.
